- **self**: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility (13/2)

## Structure and components

- [statement] A compound-index prefix consists of consecutive fields starting at the first index field. A sort matching such a prefix can use its ordering; a filter using the index does not by itself establish sort compatibility. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-index-usage-and-mongodb-explain-part-1/, https://github.com/OneUptime/blog/blob/master/posts/2026-01-30-mongodb-compound-index-strategies/README.md

## How it works

- [statement] A non-prefix sort subset can use index order when all preceding index fields have equality predicates. With {a:1,b:1,c:1}, find({a:5}).sort({b:1,c:1}) qualifies; omitting equality on a generally prevents that suffix from supplying global order through one scan. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md, https://github.com/OneUptime/blog/blob/master/posts/2026-01-30-mongodb-compound-index-strategies/README.md
- [statement] When an equality predicate fixes the leading field, a single remaining sort field can use either scan direction. For {type:1,timestamp:1}, find({type:"click"}).sort({timestamp:-1}) can use the same index as the ascending timestamp query. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://github.com/OneUptime/blog/blob/master/posts/2026-01-30-mongodb-compound-index-strategies/README.md

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use explain to distinguish index access from order provision: IXSCAN identifies index access, while an explicit SORT indicates additional sorting. Merely seeing an index scan is insufficient evidence that the index supplies the requested order. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://github.com/OneUptime/blog/blob/master/posts/2026-01-30-mongodb-compound-index-strategies/README.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] For an unconstrained compound sort, sort fields must occur in index field order. An index {a:1,b:-1} can provide {a:1,b:-1} or {a:-1,b:1}, but cannot provide {a:1,b:1}, {a:-1,b:-1}, or the reordered sort {b:-1,a:1}. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound/sort-order.md, https://github.com/OneUptime/blog/blob/master/posts/2026-01-30-mongodb-compound-index-strategies/README.md, https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-index-usage-and-mongodb-explain-part-1/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] For sort preservation, equality fields generally precede sort fields, and range fields follow them. A highly selective range can instead justify ERS and a subsequent blocking sort, so ESR is a guideline rather than a guarantee of the fastest plan. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://github.com/OneUptime/blog/blob/master/posts/2026-01-30-mongodb-compound-index-strategies/README.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A compound index orders entries lexicographically by its declared field sequence. Field order therefore affects which query and sort patterns it can serve efficiently. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/want-mongodb-performance-you-will-need-to-add-and-remove-indexes/, https://github.com/OneUptime/blog/blob/master/posts/2026-01-30-mongodb-compound-index-strategies/README.md
- [statement] A leading index prefix can supply sort order without equality predicates on those sort fields; for example, {a:1,b:1,c:1,d:1} supports sorting by {a:1,b:1} or {a:-1,b:-1}. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound/sort-order.md
- [statement] A range predicate does not universally prevent index-provided sorting. With {a:1,b:1,c:1,d:1}, find({a:{$gt:4}}).sort({a:1,b:1}) preserves index order; a range on an omitted preceding field does not generally provide global order for a later sort field. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md
- [statement] Small $in lists used with sort can be expanded into equality-like scans whose outputs are combined by SORT_MERGE; this does not remove the need for compatible suffix sort fields and directions. Larger lists can behave like ranges, preventing later index fields from providing sort order. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://github.com/OneUptime/blog/blob/master/posts/2026-01-30-mongodb-compound-index-strategies/README.md
- [statement] SERVER-14070 records a historical planner defect where {a:1,b:1} and find({a:1,b:1}).sort({b:1}) unnecessarily required sorting. The issue lists fixes in 2.6.11 and 2.8.0-rc3; this is historical evidence, not a claim that modern versions retain the bug. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-14070 · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility
- [statement] A range predicate does not universally disqualify index-provided sorting. For {a:1,b:1}, find({a:{$gt:4}}).sort({a:1,b:1}) retains index order; the difficulty is skipping a varying preceding key while sorting a later key alone. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-index-usage-and-mongodb-explain-part-1/
- [statement] Inference for SORT_MERGE: equality expansion can expose ordered suffix streams, but it does not remove the suffix field-order and direction requirements. Qualify each branch against those requirements before attributing a missing blocking sort to an ordered merge. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound/sort-order.md · keywords: Compound-index prefix and sort-direction compatibility · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md, https://github.com/OneUptime/blog/blob/master/posts/2026-01-30-mongodb-compound-index-strategies/README.md
